title: Durable webhook claims so a post-restart replay cannot re-decline a lead
acceptance: claim(k) -> true; settle(k); simulate a process restart (drop every in-memory handle, reopen the same KP_DB_PATH) -> claim(k) -> false: a finished delivery stays finished across a restart

claim(k) -> true; a second claim(k) inside the lease, same process -> false: the mark is a uniqueness-enforced write (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT with a changes check), not a read-then-write

body:
## Summary
Move the webhook idempotency claim from a process-local Map into a SQLite row with two states (in-flight under a lease, done under a bounded horizon), so the replay the edge drain and pull pass are DESIGNED to produce after a crash is absorbed instead of re-filing - and a knockout-failed applicant is never sent a second rejection. Adopts the open leftover 'Persist webhook idempotency claims across process restart' (M, risk 4, gate architecture, route human, leftover-develop-2026-09-17).

## Description
Three doors reach the same intake core: the public inbound route, the pull pass and the edge drain. Two of them are at-least-once by construction - the drain acks after apply and the pull pass adopts its cursor after a clean page - and both justify that choice by pointing at the idempotency key. But the key lives in `const claims = new Map()`: the exact event that makes a replay happen (the process dying between apply and ack) is the event that empties the dedupe. The email dedupe below it covers accepted leads only; the knockout branch in lead-intake.ts has no entry to dedupe against, so a replayed KO lead records a second decline and dispatches a second rejection email to a real candidate. The fix is the registry's third posture (at-least-once + deduplicated effects): a uniqueness-enforced mark in the store that already holds the effects, with a lease so a crash MID-work re-runs rather than drops, a settle() that turns the mark into 'done', a bounded done-horizon with a lazy sweep, fail-closed on store fault, and an edge key namespaced by pairing so a re-provisioned edge whose sequence restarts is not mistaken for a replay. The table holds only token-namespaced hashes and provider ids, so it is tenancy-EXEMPT with the same reasoning billing_events carries (a globally-unique delivery identity), stated in tenancy.ts.

## Flow
1. db/webhook-claims.ts: `webhook_claims(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, state TEXT, expires_at INTEGER)`; claim = INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE ... WHERE expires_at <= now, success iff changes === 1; settle flips state to done with the long horizon; release deletes; sweep deletes expired rows at most once a minute.
2. webhook-idempotency.ts keeps `claimWebhookIdempotency` / `releaseWebhookIdempotency` / `webhookIdempotencyKey`, adds `settleWebhookIdempotency`, delegates to the store; a store throw propagates so the door answers 5xx.
3. inbound-lead.ts, the multipart route and the agent-report route call settle() after the side effects commit.
4. edge-drain.ts derives its key as `edge:<sha256(edge url) prefix>:<seq>` and its header comment stops claiming a guarantee it did not have.
5. core.ts creates the table; tenancy.ts lists it EXEMPT with its reason; the comms feature doc (the doc feature-doc-map.json couples to inbound-lead.ts and edge-*.ts) names the durable claim and its horizon.

## Expected impact
A crash or restart during a drain or pull page no longer duplicates candidate-facing effects: no second knockout rejection email, no second `re_applied` event, no inflated liveness receipt. The edge drain's documented guarantee becomes true. Agent-report replays stop leaning on downstream upserts alone. Whole defect class closed: 'duplicates appear only after a restart' (delivery-guarantees / guarantee-selection).

## Evaluation
Claim: webhook deduplication survives a process restart without turning a mid-work crash into a lost lead.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - node:test cases above (store unit tests with an injected clock, a restart simulated by reopening the same KP_DB_PATH, and an intake replay test counting ko_declined rows and outbox rows), plus npm run test:unit, lint, tsc, docs:check.
Result: pending build
Gate: architecture

title: Scope the Analytics tab to one role, with every unscopable figure withheld
acceptance: fixture: events on entries of job A and job B in one workspace -> pipelineAnalytics(null, { jobId: A }, ws).momentum, .automation and .offers count ONLY job A's events (event rows joined to pipeline_entries.job_id through entry_id), while the no-jobId call is byte-identical to today

body:
## Summary
Give the Analytics tab the axis a hiring manager actually asks about - one requisition - end to end: a `?job=` scope that the route, the prior window, the cache and every panel honour, entered from a role-table row and carried by the copy-view link, with the figures that cannot be honestly scoped to one role withheld and named instead of silently mis-divided. Adopts the open leftover 'Job selector that scopes the whole Analytics tab to one req' (M, impact 9, leftover-develop-2026-09-17) and grows it by the correctness work its premise hid.

## Description
The store grew a jobId option (db/analytics.ts:317) but stopped at the cohort SELECT: momentum, automation impact and the offer leg read pipeline_events by workspace only, and two cost figures divide workspace- or account-wide numerators by the now job-scoped hire count. So simply wiring the leftover's selector would ship a role view whose cost-per-hire is inflated by every other role's spend. The route never passes the job, the prior-window slice has no job axis (deltas would compare a role with the whole team), the memo key would cross-serve scoped and unscoped payloads, and the role table cannot even name a job because byJob groups by title. Today a recruiter who wants 'how is the Backend req doing' either reads team-wide numbers or leaves for the board with a title search. After: a row action scopes the whole tab to that role; the header shows a clearable scope chip; event-derived panels join through entry_id; spend and compute per-hire read as withheld-with-reason in role view (not-measurable-versus-zero); the window switcher and deltas keep working; the view link shares exactly this role-and-window.

## Flow
1. db/analytics.ts: job-scoped event reads via `entry_id IN (SELECT id FROM pipeline_entries WHERE job_id = ? AND workspace_id = ?)`; costPerHireCzk and computeCost.costPerHireUsd null under a job with `jobScope: { jobId, jobTitle, withheld: [...] }`; byJob keyed by job_id carrying jobId; pipelineAnalyticsPrior takes jobId.
2. analytics-cache.ts: the key gains a job field through optionalKeyField so null and every job id are distinct.
3. api/analytics/route.ts: parse `?job=` (trimmed, length-capped), pass to both reads and the memo.
4. analyticsJobScope.ts (pure): parseJobParam, the withheld-figure labels, the scope-note choice; AnalyticsTab reads `job` beside `win` and adds it to the fetch URL.
5. AnalyticsHeader shows the scope chip with clear; the metric-pack link is labelled workspace-wide while a role is in scope; AnalyticsByRoleTable adds 'Analyse this role' per row; analyticsViewUrl carries job.
6. Four catalogs, analytics feature doc.

## Expected impact
The most common analytics question (one req's funnel, TTH, momentum, deltas) becomes answerable in one click without leaving the tab, and it is shareable as a link. It closes a latent correctness trap in the store (a job-scoped call today returns inflated per-hire cost and unscoped momentum/automation/offers) before any caller can trip on it. Role rows stop merging two reqs that share a title.

## Evaluation
Claim: a job-scoped Analytics view is correct for every figure it shows and honest about the ones it cannot scope.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - node:test over db/analytics (fixture with two jobs' entries and events), analytics-cache keying, the route handler, analyticsViewLink and analyticsJobScope; then tsc, lint, i18n:check, test:unit.
Result: pending build
Gate: contract
